C1.note: Most results characterise welfare-maximising franchises. Appendix B (Propositions 12-13, discussed in the main text) characterises equilibrium franchises.

C2.2.quote: each agent is affected by a social binary decision (0 or 1)
C2.2.note: The input is a binary opinion (0/1) for or against a single decision.

C2.3.quote: Each agent’s utility is denoted U (i, C) and depends on her success.
C2.3.note: Opinions and utilities/stakes are attributed to agents.

C5.1.quote: the planner seeks to maximise its expected value
C5.1.note: Expected aggregate welfare and ex ante Pareto superiority are used in results.

C5.2.note: Welfare depends on whether opinion Xi, which is also the majority-vote input, matches the outcome. No statement relates the input to a held attitude.

VOT.quote_behav: is decided by a majority vote among members of C
VOT.note: Votes equal opinions by the formal model. In Appendix B, voters approve the franchises they are better off under.

DES.note: The constitutional planner designs the electorate of the rule, and the paper models his objective (expected aggregate welfare) explicitly. He knows the distribution of opinions but not the realised opinions.

C1.reason: Appendix B characterises equilibrium franchises (Propositions 12-13), the appendix is in scope, and the main text discusses these results, so EQ applies alongside the primary WD.

C5.2.reason: Welfare is evaluated through success defined as agreement of Xi with the outcome, Xi is itself the argument of the majority rule, and no submission or sincerity statement is given, so the evaluation is on the input with no stated relation.

C6.DES.reason: The planner chooses the franchise, i.e. part of the voting rule itself, with an explicitly modelled objective, which matches the DES type.

C6.ORG.reason: The only choosing authority is the constitutional planner, already coded as DES, so no separate organiser acts in the model.

C8.1.reason: Beyond the planner's optimisation problem, Appendix B uses a distinct stability concept (weak Condorcet winner among franchises), which fits OTH.

C8.2.reason: The paper explicitly defines and names its concepts, both optimal franchise and, in Definitions 5-6, equilibrium franchise.
